name: ai-debugger-inc

tools.name: init
tools.description:
🚀 **REQUIRED FIRST STEP** - Initialize debugging context and get language-specific examples.

This is the mandatory entry point for debugging. You MUST call this before any other debugging operation. It provides:
- Language-specific examples (Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java)
- Framework-aware patterns (pytest, jest, django, spring, etc.)
- Workspace-aware configuration discovery
- Clear usage examples with exact syntax

mode.description: Debug mode: 'launch' (start new process), 'attach' (attach to PID), 'remote_attach' (attach to host:port). Default: launch

framework.description: Optional framework (pytest, jest, django, spring, etc.)

workspace_root.description: Root directory of the workspace for discovering launch.json and project context

workspace_roots.description: Multiple workspace roots for multi-root workspaces (e.g., microservices). Use this instead of workspace_root when debugging across multiple projects.

launch_config_name.description: Name of VS Code launch configuration to reference

verbose.description: Include educational content (key concepts, examples). Default: false for concise responses

tools.name: session_start
tools.description:
🚀 Create and start a debug session (requires init to be called first).

Supports launch/attach modes for debugging.

target.description: ENTRYPOINT file/exec that starts execution and triggers the codepath you want to debug. This is NOT where you set breakpoints - use the 'breakpoints' parameter for those. Example: target='main.py' starts app, breakpoints can be in utils/helper.py, models/user.py, etc.

pid.description: Process ID to attach to (for local attach mode)

host.description: Host to connect to (for remote attach mode)

port.description: Port to connect to (for remote attach mode)

log_message.description: Optional log message instead of pausing

breakpoints.description: Initial breakpoints as objects with 'file' and 'line' fields. Can be in ANY files, often DIFFERENT from the target. The target starts execution, breakpoints pause where you want to debug. Ex: [{'file': 'src/models/user.py', 'line': 42}, {'file': 'utils/validator.py', 'line': 15, 'condition': 'x > 0'}]

runtime_path.description: Path to the language runtime/interpreter. For Python: path to python executable (e.g., /path/to/venv/bin/python). For JavaScript: path to node executable. For Java: JAVA_HOME path. If not provided, auto-detected from target path when possible.

source_paths.description: Additional source directories for resolving file paths. Used for remote debugging where debug adapter returns paths that don't exist locally (e.g., JAR-internal paths like 'trino-main.jar!/io/trino/Foo.java'). Each path should be a local directory containing source files.

session_id.description: Optional session ID (generated if not provided)

subscribe_events.description: Events to subscribe to for notifications. 'terminated' and 'breakpoint' are always auto-subscribed. Options: 'exception' (any exception occurred)

tools.name: execute
tools.description:
Execute the program with different actions and capabilities.

Actions:
- 'run': Start execution from beginning
- 'continue': Continue from current position (default)

Enhanced features:
- Smart execution until specific conditions
- Output collection and analysis
- Automatic breakpoint management

jump_target.description: Jump to this location (``file:line``) - for jump action

wait_for_stop.description: Wait for breakpoint/stop event. Auto-enabled when breakpoints exist (default: auto)

tools.name: step
tools.description:
Step through code execution.

Actions:
- 'over': Execute line without entering functions (default)
- 'into': Enter function calls
- 'out': Complete current function

tools.name: inspect
tools.description:
Inspect program state during debugging.

Available modes:
- 'locals': Local variables (default)
- 'globals': Global variables
- 'stack': Call stack with frames
- 'threads': All thread states
- 'expression': Evaluate specific expression
- 'all': Complete state snapshot

tools.name: breakpoint
tools.description:
Manage breakpoints. Supports conditions (condition='x>5'), hit counts (hit_condition='>3' to skip first 3 hits), and logpoints (log_message='val={x}').

Actions:
- 'set': Set a breakpoint (default)
- 'remove': Remove a breakpoint
- 'list': List all breakpoints
- 'clear_all': Remove all breakpoints
- 'watch': Set watchpoint (Java only)
- 'unwatch': Remove watchpoint (Java only)

column.description: Column number for precise breakpoint placement (for minified code)

hit_condition.description: Hit count condition (e.g., '> 5' to break after 5 hits)

access_type.description: Access type for watch action: 'read', 'write', or 'readWrite'

tools.name: variable
tools.description:
Enhanced variable operations with live patching capabilities.

Actions:
- 'get': Evaluate expression (default)
- 'set': Set variable value
- 'patch': Live code patching for rapid iteration (replaces aidb.fix)

Examples:
- variable('get', expression='user.name')
- variable('set', name='debug_mode', value='True')
- variable('patch', name='calculate_tax', code='return amount * 0.08')

tools.name: session
tools.description:
Comprehensive session lifecycle management.

**Actions:**
• `status`: Show current session status (default)
• `list`: List all active sessions
• `stop`: Stop current/specified session
• `restart`: Restart session with same configuration
• `switch`: Switch to different session

tools.name: config
tools.description:
Configuration and environment management.

**Actions:**
• `show`: Show current configuration (default)
• `env`: Show/set environment variables
• `launch`: Discover and manage VS Code launch.json configurations
• `capabilities`: Show debugging capabilities for languages (replaces aidb.capabilities)
• `adapters`: Check debug adapter installation status

**Examples:**
• config('env') - Show AIDB_* environment variables
• config('launch') - List available launch configurations
• config('adapters') - Show installed debug adapters
• config('capabilities', language='python') - Python debugging features

tools.name: context
tools.description:
Rich debugging context and intelligent next-step suggestions.

Provides:
- Current debugging state and session memory
- Recent operations and their outcomes
- Intelligent next-step recommendations
- Cross-tool workflow suggestions
- Debugging history and patterns

tools.name: run_until
tools.description:
Run until a specific location with temporary breakpoints.

Sets one-time breakpoints that are automatically removed after being hit.
Useful for quickly running to specific locations without permanent breakpoints.

Enhanced features:
- Multiple target locations
- Conditional temporary breakpoints
- Automatic cleanup

location.description: Primary target location (file.py:line or line number)

tools.name: adapter
tools.description:
Consolidated adapter management with action-based operations

**Actions:**
• `download`: Download and install a specific language adapter (requires language)
• `download_all`: Download and install all available adapters (language ignored)
• `list`: List installed adapters and status (language optional)

**Management:**
Downloads debug adapters from GitHub releases to ~/.aidb/adapters/. Versions match current project. Validates language support dynamically.

**Aliases:** install→download, install_all→download_all, status/show→list

**Usage:** Install missing adapters when encountering AdapterNotFoundError messages.

version.description: Specific version to download (download action only). Defaults to latest version matching current project

force.description: Force re-download if already installed (download/download_all actions). Use when adapters need updating or are corrupted
